policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Reduced the total allowable catch (TAC) for horse mackerel for the 2026 fishing season by 5% to 197,000 metric tons, citing it as a "proactive" measure. According to the ministry, the latest scientific survey estimates the horse mackerel biomass at 784,011 tonnes, and while the biomass remains within sustainable biological limits, the assessment identifies a recent decline that necessitates a prudent and responsive management approach. However, the announcement itself proved controversial. The Ministry did not publicly announce the total allowable catch when the 2026 horse mackerel fishing season started on 1 January, instead sending letters to rights holders stating that the TAC had been reduced by 5%. The total non-commercial harvesting quota for the 2026 season is at 69,706.01 metric tonnes, which constitutes 35% of the TAC, split between freezer and wet-landed operations. This government reservation of one-third of the total catch created operational planning difficulties for commercial operators.
